A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BeamLoRA work. All 13 pages in each version, including Appendices A and B, are readable, and corresponding equations, tables and figures can be matched.

before.justification: Tables 1–3 report original BeamLoRA benchmark and ablation results. Appendix B includes original hyperparameter sensitivity and computational efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original BeamLoRA experiments on mathematical reasoning, code generation and commonsense reasoning, together with ablation, sensitivity and efficiency results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain learned rank scores, pruning and expansion using historical parameters and optimizer states, dynamic Top-P thresholds, and inference merging. Replacing 'copy' with 'assign' does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MetaMathQA, CodeFeedback105K and Commonsense170K and evaluate the same 12 math, code and commonsense benchmarks. Naming evaluation codebases in v2 does not establish additional test coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–2 and the efficiency comparisons in Figures 8–9. Newly cited methods such as Light-PEFT and MoRA are not added to the evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 revises the stated Mistral-7B learning rate for PEFT methods other than ReLoRA from 3e-4 to 6e-5 on math and code tasks; LLaMA2-7B remains at 3e-4. This is a limited reported settings revision and does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The component ablations, rank-importance and pruning analyses, rank sweep, Appendix B.1 hyperparameter sweeps, and Appendix B.2 efficiency comparisons are retained. Expanded captions summarize existing analyses.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly states that results are averaged over three runs. v1 provides no repeated-run count. This adds reporting information without establishing an increase in runs; no seeds, dispersion estimates or statistical tests are added.

E6.justification: Section 4.3 corrects the reported LLaMA2-13B gain over LoRA from 0.4% to 0.3%, consistent with the unchanged Table 2 averages of 84.0 and 83.7. Benchmark scores, ablation results and plotted findings otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 removes the explicit x∈R^d and y∈R^d declarations after Equation 1, eliminating the inconsistent input-dimension specification for W0∈R^{d×k}. This is a small mathematical specification correction; the equations and derivations are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same rank-importance motivation, BeamLoRA contribution, and effectiveness claims across three models and 12 benchmarks. The headline 1.57-point gain over full fine-tuning is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning balanced rank utilization, reduced benefits at small ranks, and difficulties extending the method to full-parameter training remain unchanged. Caption additions and the revised model-size discussion restate existing explanations.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised code release with a stated repository link and identifies MetaMathQA, EvalPlus and LLM-Adapters as evaluation codebases in Appendix A.2. It also supplies the revised model-specific learning-rate information.

R1.justification: Six references are added, covering Mixture of Hidden-Dimensions Transformer, LEMON, Light-PEFT, MoRA, EvalPlus and Qwen2.5. These modestly extend the citations while retaining the existing positioning relative to LoRA variants and pruning/expansion methods.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, lightly rewrites related-work prose, and adds acknowledgments. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 5 and Table 3 move between columns, and efficiency Figures 8–9 move to page 13. Several captions expand. Figure graphics, axes and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reproducibility and reporting accuracy through code-access information, named evaluation implementations, more specific learning-rate documentation, three-run averaging disclosure, and the corrected commonsense gain. These provide limited transparency and clarity gains while the underlying method and empirical evidence remain essentially unchanged.
